claims.text: As-cast or equilibrated high-entropy alloys generally exhibit complex multicomponent phase structures.
Simultaneous high-temperature imaging and calorimetry enable accurate determination of melting temperature across diverse high-entropy alloys.
Simultaneous high-temperature imaging and calorimetry enable accurate determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy across diverse high-entropy alloys.
Simultaneous high-temperature imaging and calorimetry enable accurate determination of volume change at melting and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties.
High-penetration radiographic imaging can identify the onset and progression of melting in real time.
High-penetration radiographic imaging can reveal liquid-phase separation and remixing during alloying.
Calorimetric measurements made concurrently with imaging provide quantitative energy-input or heat-flow data.
Time-correlating imaging events with heat-flow signatures permits extraction of melting temperature.
Time-correlating imaging events with heat-flow signatures permits extraction of latent heat and fusion entropy.
The combined imaging and calorimetric signals permit extraction of the volume change associated with melting.
Radiographs can be collected at temperature increments as fine as 20 °C during a high-temperature heating and cooling cycle.
A high-temperature vacuum or inert atmosphere eliminates oxidation during the measurement.
The integrated method should produce melting temperatures and fusion parameters within experimental error of standards or independent measurements.
The integrated method significantly reduces experimental trial time relative to sequential imaging and calorimetric measurements.
The method can capture subtle microstructural transitions across the compositional variation of high-entropy alloys.
Traditional DSC and separate high-temperature imaging, when used independently, have limitations in spatial resolution, speed, or accuracy across compositional space.
Large atomic-number differences or compositional inhomogeneity may compromise imaging contrast or calorimetric calibration.
The approach is applicable primarily when imaging provides clear phase contrast that can be correlated with thermal events.
Prior neutron-imaging work demonstrates in-situ observation of melting, liquid remixing, and solidification in CoCrCu modified with Ni.
Quantitative coupling of imaging signatures to thermodynamic parameters across the full high-entropy-alloy compositional range remains unvalidated.

contradictions.description: The design proposes comparing derived volume change from both the integrated method and standard DSC, but the listed reference measurements contain no independent volumetric measurement; standard DSC alone does not directly measure volume change.
